image_description: A grey whale breaching or surfacing in blue ocean water. The head and upper back are visible, showing mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches. A large splash surrounds the emerging body. A watermark text '© Roi Hlaker' is superimposed across the center of the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is angled steeply upward and partially obscured by spray; the top of the rostrum where blowholes would be located is not clearly visible to verify count or position.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the head and back clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white callosities/barnacle patches.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the back behind the head shows a series of low humps (knuckles) rather than a single triangular dorsal fin, consistent with grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior section of the whale is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified due to occlusion by water and framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible back skin exhibits the correct mottling and barnacle distribution.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or submerged; baleen plates are internal/underwater structures not visible in this external breach shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located ventrally and are completely submerged or occluded by the angle of the breach and water splash.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is entirely underwater and outside the frame of the visible subject.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-contrast white patches on the grey skin visually correspond to the rough texture of callosities/barnacles typical of the species.

artifact_observations.location: Center horizontal band overlaying sky and water
artifact_observations.reasoning: The watermark text '© Roi Hlaker' exhibits slight character deformation and uneven baseline alignment, particularly in the letters 'H', 'l', and 'k'. While legible, the edges show minor melting into the background, typical of AI-generated or poorly rendered text overlays.

The water texture appears overly uniform and 'painterly' with a lack of fine-grained foam detail in the splash. The transition between the whale's skin and the water shows slight blurring/haloing rather than sharp displacement.
